text: Let (Ω, 𝒜, μ) be a probability space, let 𝒳 be a nonempty measurable space, and let X : Ω → 𝒳 be measurable. Let H be a nonempty separable, first-countable topological parameter space, and let (f_h : 𝒳 → ℝ)_{h∈H} be measurable functions. Assume that |f_h(x)| ≤ b for all h and x, where b>0, and that h ↦ f_h(x) is continuous for each x∈𝒳. Fix an integer n≥1 and ε≥0. Draw ω_1,…,ω_n independently with law μ and set S_k=X(ω_k). Define P f_h = ∫_Ω f_h(X(ω)) dμ(ω), P_n f_h(S) = (1/n)∑_{k=1}^n f_h(S_k), and U_n(S)=sup_{h∈H}|P_n f_h(S)−P f_h|. For a fixed sample S, define the absolute empirical Rademacher complexity R̂_n(f;S) = 2^(−n)∑_{σ∈{−1,1}^n} sup_{h∈H}|(1/n)∑_{k=1}^n σ_k f_h(S_k)|, and define R_n(f;μ,X)=E_{ω∼μ^n}[R̂_n(f;X∘ω)]. Then μ^n({ω : U_n(X∘ω) ≥ 2 R_n(f;μ,X)+ε}) ≤ exp(−n ε²/(2b²)). The complexity in this statement contains an absolute value inside the supremum; it is the expected complexity, not the empirical complexity of the observed sample.
